content: Title: CYP3A4-Mediated Drug Interactions in Elderly Polypharmacy Patients: A Systematic Review. Authors: Zhang L, Chen M, Huang R. Journal: Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics. PMID: 36891234. Year: 2023. Abstract: CYP3A4 is responsible for the metabolism of approximately 50% of all prescribed medications. In elderly patients receiving five or more medications (polypharmacy), the probability of at least one CYP3A4-mediated drug-drug interaction exceeds 80%. This systematic review of 47 studies (n=12,847 patients) found that the most clinically significant CYP3A4 interactions in polypharmacy settings involved macrolide antibiotics (clarithromycin, erythromycin) combined with statins, calcium channel blockers, or anticoagulants. Clarithromycin co-administration with atorvastatin increased statin AUC by 4.4-fold (95% CI: 3.2-5.8), while the combination with warfarin increased INR by an average of 1.8 units. Age-related decline in CYP3A4 activity (approximately 30% reduction by age 70) further potentiates these interactions. The review concludes that systematic CYP3A4 interaction screening should be mandatory in polypharmacy auditing systems.
